content:
Google is set to limit the Gemini models available to free users and AI Plus subscribers following an adjustment to compute usage in May this year.

According to support documents updated this week, Gemini App users without a Google AI subscription will only be able to use the (3.5) Flash-Lite model. Starting from October 9, users without a paid Gemini subscription will no longer be able to use (3.6) Flash or (3.1) Pro.

On the other hand, AI Plus subscribers will only be able to use Flash-Lite and Flash, while Pro will no longer be offered. These users, who pay a monthly fee of US$4.99, will "receive an email explaining when these changes will take effect."

Gemini Model Google AI Plan Flash-Lite Flash Pro Without a plan ✓ X X AI Plus ✓ ✓ X AI Pro ✓ ✓ ✓ AI Ultra ✓ ✓ ✓

AI Pro and AI Ultra have not been downgraded. Instead, customers paying US$19.99 per month will gain access to the Deep Think option, a "maximum parallel reasoning" feature currently only available with plans priced at US$99.99 and US$199.99 per month.

Gemini 3.1 Pro on AI Ultra comes with Deep Think

In October, the Gemini App also appears set to add "Low," "Medium," and "High" thinking effort options for "each available model."

Currently, you can only enable "Extended Thinking: Complex Problem Solving." These three new thinking effort options will correspond to those offered in Google AI Studio and Antigravity.

It is still unclear where Gemini 4 Argon will be positioned. Google announced earlier this week that it will first be made available to AI Ultra subscribers. The company has not indicated whether Argon will be classified as a Pro model or as a new tier above Pro.
